source.title: Don't Stop Long-Context Continual Pre-Training Too Early: An Empirical Scaling Law
source.authors: Zi-Qing Qiao; Xiao-Yue Xu; Si Zhang; Yi-Nuo Xu; Bing-Xiang He; Chao-Jun Xiao; Xu Han

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling-law and extrapolation behavior in long-context continual pre-training, a distinct training setting, using LongPPL as its long-context performance measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own LongPPL scaling, held-out-scale extrapolation, fixed-model trajectory fits, and downstream evaluations; these are recorded below. Claims about scaling laws in related work are citations, not results here. It does not test a fixed-compute optimal allocation, architecture variation at fixed parameter count, or other modalities.
record.test_reason: The study fits and extrapolates an additive Chinchilla-style power law for log(LongPPL) in long-context continual pre-training, a new training regime. It reports held-out-scale extrapolation, comparisons of functional forms and offsets, and downstream trends with LCCP budget. The target is a loss on about 1.4% of tokens selected for long-context dependence, not ordinary held-out pretraining loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that an additive power law with a (negative) free offset predicts log(LongPPL) across LCCP scales and budgets. Under Constant-Last4 it predicts the ~100B-token trajectory of the S5 model (821M non-embedding, 1.22B total). Downstream long-context and agentic gains persist after 128K extension and SFT. They explicitly call the law finite-range, not asymptotic, and note that checkpoint merging's advantage does not consistently persist through SFT.
record.recipe_differences: The paper fits a custom additive law for log(LongPPL) using non-embedding parameters and separate short- and long-context token budgets in LCCP. It does not reproduce the original studies' standard held-out pretraining-loss or fixed-compute allocation analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Extrapolation performance depends on functional form and offset constraint (R6, R7, R17). Observation protocol affects measured LongPPL: Constant-Last4 more closely matches linear-decay than raw constant-rate checkpoints (R18, R19). The fitted coefficients and exponents differ across linear-decay and Constant-Last4 fits (R16).

fits_no_version.finding: Along the S5 trajectory, the log-elasticity ratio of LongPPL to ShortPPL falls from about 3.35 at 5N to 2.22 at 120N; LongPPL improves faster than ShortPPL throughout.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In long-context continual pre-training, long-context-dependent tokens improve faster with training tokens than local tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: A fixed-head retrieval-head score plateaus after about 30N while RULER-32K keeps improving to 120N.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mechanistic retrieval-head metrics saturate earlier than behavioral long-context gains during LCCP.

record.problems: The central target is LongPPL on selected long-context-sensitive tokens, not ordinary pretraining cross-entropy. The experiments cover five model scales up to 821M non-embedding parameters, and the authors explicitly call the fitted law finite-range rather than asymptotic. Downstream evaluations are largely presented as plots; some task results fluctuate, and the supplementary doubled-SFT experiment uses one data seed.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported downstream aggregate values could be read from the supplied figures, so those trend results are recorded as figure-only rows. Detailed per-subtask figure values and the large set of individual training configurations are not itemized; the paper's explicit aggregate descriptions and held-out fit results are retained.

untested.parts: Not tested. No ordinary held-out pretraining cross-entropy is fitted; only LongPPL (and ShortPPL) on selected tokens in continual pre-training. N spans under one order of magnitude in the fits.
Extrapolation beyond about 3.3x in parameters and about 8x in LCCP tokens. Orders-of-magnitude extrapolation and standard pretraining loss are untested.
Not tested: no fixed-compute sweep or compute-optimal allocation.
Not tested: depth and width co-vary with size; no fixed-N shape comparison.
Other modalities, repeated data, and fine-tuning/transfer as scaling regimes.
No quantitative prediction of downstream scores from scale or loss. Only trends with LCCP budget for one model (S5) are reported.

missing.what: Saturating power-law fit of ShortPPL (and LongPPL) versus Dl along the S5 trajectory, used for the elasticity comparison
RULER-32K subtask numbers: niah_multikey_2 51.20→71.20, multivalue 10.20→28.75, multiquery 18.75→45.00 (5N→120N, Last4); multikey_3, VT and CWE stay near floor
RULER-128K subtask numbers: multikey_2 8→25 (Last4), multiquery 26.75→36.25 with a peak of 45.25 at 80N
Training-set R² across all formulas (0.963–0.995) does not distinguish forms that extrapolate very differently

record.verdict_notes: V1 links were removed because LongPPL is a selected-token loss in continual pre-training, so the evidence is placed under V5. The extrapolation range is modest (about 3.3x N, about 8x Dl), so V2 support is limited to that range. R18 and R19 are protocol validations of the study's own method. The low prefix-fit R² may partly reflect the narrow variance of the held-out values, given MAPE under 1.2%.

versions.untested_parts: The measurement is log(LongPPL), a held-out long-context metric on selected tokens, not ordinary held-out pretraining cross-entropy. It does not test scaling with training compute.
Extrapolation is tested for LongPPL in LCCP, not for ordinary pretraining cross-entropy or arbitrary larger runs.
No fixed-compute budget sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is tested.
No comparison varies depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
Tests long-context continual pre-training, not other modalities, repeated data, or fine-tuning/transfer as settings for the scaling law.
Reports downstream trends across LCCP budgets, but does not fit or validate a quantitative mapping from pretraining loss to downstream performance.
Compares selected functional forms and learning-rate protocols. It does not test compute-optimal allocation, parameter-counting conventions, or a broad set of datasets and training schedules.

rows.subject: S1–S4 configurations (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: non-embedding parameters range from 31M to 245M for S1–S4
rows.operation_detail: Varied model size, short-context pretraining tokens Ds, and LCCP tokens Dl; fitted an additive power law to log(LongPPL).
rows.measure: Power-law trend of log(LongPPL) against N, Ds, and Dl
rows.value: Observed trends were described as consistent with power-law decay with an offset. The fitted form was log(LongPPL) = A N^-α + Bs Ds^-βs + Bl Dl^-βl + C.
rows.note: This is the paper's LCCP-specific held-out LongPPL metric, not standard pretraining loss.
rows.check: LongPPL is a continual-pretraining loss on 1.42% of tokens selected for long-context dependence, not held-out pretraining loss, so the row does not bear on V1. N spans less than one order of magnitude (31M–245M).

rows.subject: S1–S5 fits (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: LCCP under linear-decay and Constant-Last4 schedules
rows.operation_detail: Compared fitted exponents and offsets across the two training/observation protocols.
rows.measure: Fitted parameters of the additive law
rows.value: For linear-decay fits, C = -0.60 and -0.82; for Constant-Last4 fits, C = -0.71 and -0.61. Exponents also differ across fits; e.g. βl is 0.235262, 0.234577, 0.223068, and 0.225344, respectively.
rows.note: The paper also states that the free offset makes this a finite-range empirical law, not a valid asymptotic law.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix A.5, Table 11: linear-decay offsets −0.600638/−0.817910; Constant-Last4 offsets −0.710403/−0.613778.

rows.subject: S1–S5 fits (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: LCCP under linear-decay and Constant-Last4 schedules
rows.operation_detail: Compared zero/nonnegative-offset fits with a free-offset fit.
rows.value: The no-offset and nonnegative-offset versions gave R² = 0.7995 and MAPE = 3.62% on S4; R² = -0.1031 and MAPE = 9.05% on S5 for linear-decay. For Constant-Last4, they gave R² = 0.9354 and MAPE = 1.89% on S4; R² = -4.0917 and MAPE = 11.01% on S5.
rows.locator: Appendix A.2, Tables 3–4; Appendix A.2 text
rows.note: These results show strong dependence of extrapolation quality on the offset constraint; the paper interprets the fitted negative offset as a finite-range correction.
rows.check: For V7 the effect (extrapolation depends strongly on the offset constraint) is fully shown, so the state should be observed, not partial. The row also bears on V5: the power-law form extrapolates only with a negative free offset.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix A.2, Tables 3–4 and offset-constraints paragraph: both constrained variants give identical results within each protocol; linear-decay S4 R²=0.7995, MAPE=3.62%.
